x = (horizontal % ÷ 100) × page width

howTo: Click “Choose PDF file” and select the document you want to edit.
Pick a tool: text, image, rectangle, or freehand drawing.
For freehand, draw on the pad with your mouse or finger, then clear and redraw if needed.
Set the page, position and size for each element, and click “Add element” to queue it.
Click “Apply edits”, then download the edited PDF.
keyFacts: Freehand strokes are drawn on an HTML canvas with pointer events, then exported as a transparent PNG.
The canvas is 600 × 220 pixels; your drawing is scaled to the width percentage you choose on the page.
Text uses the standard Helvetica font, which every PDF reader supports.
Rectangle elements are outlines only — they frame an area without covering it.
All elements are queued first and applied to the PDF in one pass when you click “Apply edits”.

edit-pdf.workedExample:
Draw a signature on the 600 × 220 pad and place it 25% wide on an A4 page (595.28 pt) at X 65%, Y 8%:
drawing width = 0.25 × 595.28 = 148.82 pt
drawing height = 148.82 ÷ (600 ÷ 220) = 148.82 ÷ 2.7272 = 54.57 pt
x = 0.65 × 595.28 = 386.93 pt from the left
y = 0.08 × 841.89 = 67.35 pt from the bottom
The signature lands bottom-right at about 149 × 55 pt.
